description:
FILED s469bg (Opus, 2026-09-05) from the #1035 step-2 review fix.

WHAT.  A lexical that SPANS a package boundary is promoted to a cell and
declared TWICE: once unqualified in the declaring segment, and once
package-QUALIFIED in each later segment whose reader sits in another package
(ir-spec 2b.3's `$Pkg::x__file__N` row).  Since #1035 step 2 the first carries
the manifest and the second does not:

    my $shared = 7;
    package Later; print "later=$shared\n";
    package main; { my $shared = 99; print "inner=$shared\n"; }

    (p-defcell $shared__file__0 (make-p-box nil) :perl "$shared" :why :spanning)
    (p-defcell main::$shared__file__0 (make-p-box nil))          <-- bare

WHY IT IS NOT A HOLE.  Both forms declare the SAME cell, and the annotated one
is in the same emitted file, so a consumer never loses the information -- it
just has to notice that the qualified spelling is the same cell, which
ir-spec 2b.3 already tells it to do.  That is why this was filed rather than
fixed in the review commit.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED THERE.  `_decl_facts` is keyed by the name the rename
recorded, which is UNQUALIFIED.  Annotating the twin means either (a) stripping
a leading `PKG::` before the manifest lookup -- a string rule that could in
principle attach a fact to a genuinely-qualified package global whose bare part
collides with a minted name (the `__file__N` suffix makes that all but
impossible, but "all but" is not a proof), or (b) recording the qualified
spelling at the SPANNING pass, which is the site that generates it and knows it
names its own cell.  (b) is the right shape and costs one registration call;
it was out of scope for a review fix whose bar was the arithmetic.

BAR IF TAKEN: the manifest arithmetic (see the s469bg record) must still read
0 unannotated, and the corpus `:perl` token count rises by the number of
qualified spanning twins.  Guard row in Pl/t/decl-facts-01.t beside the
existing `:spanning` row.
subject: the package-QUALIFIED twin declaration of a SPANNING cell carries no rename manifest -- `main::$x__file__0` prints bare where `$x__file__0` prints `:perl`/`:why`; the fact is in the same file, so it is polish, not a hole
